steps: For five square values q_n with second difference two, put D=q_1-q_0.
If D is even then q_0,q_1 have the same parity and D is divisible by four; q_2=q_0+2D+2 is then 2 or 3 modulo four, impossible for a square.
Thus D is odd and the recurrence gives q_n=q_0+nD+n(n-1).
Set x=(D-1)/2 and a=q_0-x^2, both integers, obtaining q_n=(x+n)^2+a.
Conversely an integer-offset sequence has second difference two; comparison with consecutive square values (t+n)^2 yields x=t and a=0.

steps: If A is empty, any element of the nonempty ground type witnesses 0 <= 0.
If A is nonempty and A is not {empty}, at least one member is nonempty.
The union of finitely many finite members is finite even when n is infinite.
A witness for the half-frequency conclusion in a nonempty family has positive frequency, hence belongs to that finite union.
Thus the formal target's additional empty-family allowance is harmless and its substantive part matches the finite nonempty-member formulation.
